translations.idiomatic: On returning home, he received the county magistrate with ritual severity: clerks stood until the magistrate had gone.

sentences.zh: 經縣署，降馬而趨。

translations.literal: Passing the county office, he dismounted and hurried on foot.
translations.idiomatic: He dismounted and hastened on foot past the county seat.

translations.literal: Poetry of Zu Yong, one scroll; Poetry of Li Qi, one scroll; both passed the Jinshi examination in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry of Zu Yong, 1 scroll; Poetry of Li Qi, 1 scroll; both Kaiyuan jinshi.

sentences.zh: 孟浩然詩集三卷弟洗然。

translations.literal: Collected Poetry of Meng Haoran, three scrolls; his younger brother Xiran.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Poetry of Meng Haoran, 3 scrolls; his younger brother Xiran.

sentences.zh: 宜城王士源所次，皆三卷也。

translations.literal: Arranged by Wang Shiyuan of Yicheng—all three scrolls each.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shiyuan of Yicheng arranged them, each in three scrolls.

sentences.zh: 士源別為七類。

translations.literal: Shiyuan arranged them in seven categories.
translations.idiomatic: Shiyuan divided them into seven categories.

sentences.zh: 包融詩一卷潤州延陵人。

translations.literal: Poetry of Bao Rong, one scroll; a native of Yanling in Runzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Poetry of Bao Rong, 1 scroll; from Yanling in Runzhou.

sentences.zh: 歷大理司直。

translations.literal: He served as director of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: He was director of the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 二子何、佶齊名，世稱「二包」。

translations.literal: His two sons He and Ji were equally famous, and the age called them "the Two Bao."
translations.idiomatic: His sons He and Ji were both famed—the "Two Bao."

sentences.zh: 何，字幼嗣，大曆起居舍人。

translations.literal: He, courtesy name Yousi, was attendance scribe in the Dali era.
translations.idiomatic: Bao He, courtesy name Yousi, Dali attendance scribe.

sentences.zh: 融與儲光羲皆延陵人；

translations.literal: Rong, like Chu Guangxi, was from Yanling;
translations.idiomatic: Bao Rong, like Chu Guangxi, was from Yanling;

sentences.zh: 曲阿有餘杭尉丁仙芝、緱氏主簿蔡隱丘、監察御史蔡希周、渭南尉蔡希寂、處士張彥雄張潮、校書郎張暈、吏部常選周瑀、長洲尉談戭，句容有忠王府倉曹參軍殷遙、硤石主簿樊光、橫陽主簿沈如筠，江寧有右拾遺孫處玄、處士徐延壽，丹徒有江都主簿馬挺、武進尉申堂構，十八人皆有詩名。

translations.literal: In Qu'a were the district magistrate of Yuhang Ding Xianzhi, the registrar of Gou Shi Cai Yinqiu, the investigating censor Cai Xizhou, the district magistrate of Weinan Cai Xiji, the recluses Zhang Yanxiong and Zhang Chao, the collator Zhang Yun, the regular selection officer of the Ministry of Personnel Zhou Yu, and the district magistrate of Changzhou Tan Yan; in Jurong were the warehouse clerk of the Prince of Zhong's household Yin Yao, the registrar of Qia Shi Fan Guang, and the registrar of Hengyang Shen Ruyun; in Jiangning were the right remonstrance Sun Chuxuan and the recluse Xu Yanshou; in Dantu were the registrar of Jiangdu Ma Ting and the district magistrate of Wujin Shen Tangou—eighteen men all had poetic fame.
translations.idiomatic: Eighteen poets are named across Qu'a, Jurong, Jiangning, and Dantu—from Ding Xianzhi and Cai Yinqiu to Shen Tangou.

sentences.zh: 殷璠彙次其詩，為丹楊集者。

translations.literal: Yin Pu compiled their poems into the Danyang Collection.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Pu anthologized their poems as the Danyang Collection.

sentences.zh: 皇甫冉詩集三卷字茂政，潤州丹楊人，祕書少監、集賢院脩撰彬姪也。

translations.literal: Collected Poetry of Huangfu Ran, three scrolls; courtesy name Maozheng; a native of Danyang in Runzhou; nephew of the Secretariat Vice Director and Hanlin compiler Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Poetry of Huangfu Ran, 3 scrolls; courtesy name Maozheng, from Danyang in Runzhou; nephew of Huangfu Bin.

sentences.zh: 天寶末無錫尉，避難居陽羨，後為左金吾衞兵曹參軍、左補闕，與弟曾齊名。

translations.literal: At the end of Tianbao he was district magistrate of Wuxi; he took refuge in Yangxian, later became military adjutant of the Left Golden Guard and left supplementer, and was as famous as his younger brother Zeng.
translations.idiomatic: Late Tianbao Wuxi magistrate; he fled to Yangxian, later served the Golden Guard and as left supplementer, famed alongside his brother Zeng.

sentences.zh: 曾，字孝常，歷侍御史，坐事貶徙舒州司馬，陽翟令。

translations.literal: Zeng, courtesy name Xiaochang, served as attendant censor; because of an offense he was demoted and banished as military aide of Shuzhou, then made magistrate of Yangzhai.
translations.idiomatic: Zeng, courtesy name Xiaochang, was an attendant censor; disgraced, he was exiled as Shuzhou aide and later became Yangzhai magistrate.

sentences.zh: 嚴維詩一卷字正文，越州人，祕書郎。

translations.literal: Yan Wei, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Zhengwen; a native of Yuezhou; Secretary of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Poems of Yan Wei, 1 scroll; courtesy name Zhengwen; from Yuezhou; served as Secretary of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 張繼詩一卷字懿孫，襄州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Ji, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Yisun; a native of Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Ji, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Yisun; a native of Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 大曆末，檢校祠部員外郎，分掌財賦於洪州。

translations.literal: At the end of the Dali era he was Acting Vice Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices and supervised fiscal administration at Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Dali period he served as acting Vice Director of the Bureau of Sacrifices, overseeing revenue and taxation at Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 李嘉祐詩一卷別名從一，袁州、台州二刺史。

translations.literal: Li Jiayou, Poems, one scroll; also called Congyi; Prefect of both Yuanzhou and Taizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiayou, Poems, 1 scroll, also known as Congyi; served as prefect of Yuanzhou and Taizhou.

sentences.zh: 郎士元詩一卷字君冑，中山人。

translations.literal: Lang Shiyuan, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Jungou; a native of Zhongshan.
translations.idiomatic: Poems of Lang Shiyuan, 1 scroll; courtesy name Jungou; from Zhongshan.

sentences.zh: 寶應元年，選畿縣官，詔試中書，補渭南尉，歷拾遺、郢州刺史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Baoying he was selected as a capital-district official, tested by edict at the Secretariat, appointed District Defender of Weinan, and served as Reminder and Prefect of Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In 762 he was chosen as a metropolitan district official, examined at the Secretariat by imperial order, appointed defender of Weinan, and later served as remonstrance official and prefect of Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 張南史詩一卷字季直，幽州人。

translations.literal: Zhang Nanshi, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Jizhi; a native of Youzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Nanshi, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Jizhi; from Youzhou.

sentences.zh: 以試參軍避亂居揚州楊子，再召之，未赴，卒。

translations.literal: As a trial staff officer he fled the disorders and lived at Yangzi in Yangzhou; summoned again, he did not go, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He had been a probationary staff officer; fleeing the rebellion he settled at Yangzi in Yangzhou, was summoned once more but declined to return, and died.

sentences.zh: 暢當詩二卷鄭常詩一卷蘇渙詩一卷渙少喜剽盜，善用白弩，巴蜀商人苦之，號白跖，以比莊蹻。

translations.literal: Chang Dang, Poems, two scrolls; Zheng Chang, Poems, one scroll; Su Huan, Poems, one scroll; in youth Huan delighted in robbery, was skilled with the white crossbow, merchants of Ba and Shu suffered from him, and he was called White Foot, likened to Zhuang Jue.
translations.idiomatic: Poems of Chang Dang, 2 scrolls; Poems of Zheng Chang, 1 scroll; Poems of Su Huan, 1 scroll. In his youth Huan took to banditry and excelled with the white crossbow; merchants of Ba and Shu dreaded him and nicknamed him White Foot, comparing him to Zhuang Jue.

sentences.zh: 後折節讀書，進士及第。

translations.literal: Later he reformed his conduct and studied; he passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: He later mended his ways, took up study, and passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 湖南崔瓘辟從事，瓘遇害，渙走交廣，與哥舒晃反，伏誅。

translations.literal: Cui Guan of Hunan recruited him as a staff officer; when Guan was killed, Huan fled to Jiaozhi and Guang, joined Geshu Huang in rebellion, and was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Guan of Hunan engaged him on his staff; after Guan was murdered, Huan fled to the far south, joined Geshu Huang's revolt, and was put to death.

sentences.zh: 朱灣詩集四卷李勉永平從事。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Zhu Wan, four scrolls; a staff officer under Li Mian at Yongping.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Works of Zhu Wan, 4 scrolls; he served on Li Mian's staff at Yongping.

sentences.zh: 吉中孚詩一卷楚州人，始為道士，後官校書郎，登宏辭，諫議大夫、翰林學士、戶部侍郎，判度支。

translations.literal: Ji Zhongfu, Poems, one scroll; a native of Chuzhou; at first a Daoist priest, later Proofreader of the Secretariat, passed the hongci examination, Remonstrance Official, Hanlin Academician, Vice Minister of Revenue, and supervised the fiscal administration.
translations.idiomatic: Ji Zhongfu, Poems, 1 scroll, from Chuzhou; he was first a Daoist priest, then became a proofreader, passed the hongci examination, and rose to remonstrance official, Hanlin academician, and Vice Minister of Revenue in charge of fiscal affairs.

sentences.zh: 貞元初卒。

translations.literal: He died at the beginning of the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Zhenyuan period.

sentences.zh: 朱放詩一卷字長通，襄州人，隱居剡溪。

translations.literal: Zhu Fang, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Changtong; a native of Xiangzhou; lived in seclusion on the Shan Stream.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Fang, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Changtong; from Xiangzhou; lived in reclusion on the Shan Stream.

sentences.zh: 嗣曹王皋鎮江西，辟節度參謀，貞元初召為拾遺，不就。

translations.literal: When the heir Prince of Cao, Cao Gao, governed Jiangxi, he was recruited as military adviser; at the beginning of Zhenyuan he was summoned as Reminder but did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Cao Gao governed Jiangxi, he recruited Zhu as a military adviser; in early Zhenyuan the court summoned him as remonstrance official, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 劉方平詩一卷河南人，與元魯山善，不仕。

translations.literal: Liu Fangping, Poems, one scroll; a native of Henan; was friendly with Yuan Lushan; did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Fangping, Poems, 1 scroll; from Henan; a close friend of Yuan Lushan; he never served in office.

sentences.zh: 常建詩一卷肅、代時人。

translations.literal: Chang Jian, Poems, one scroll; a man of the Suzong and Daizong eras.
translations.idiomatic: Chang Jian, Poems, 1 scroll; a poet of the Suzong and Daizong reigns.

sentences.zh: 麴信陵詩一卷章八元詩一卷睦州人，大曆進士第。

translations.literal: Qu Xinling, Poems, one scroll; Zhang Bayuan, Poems, one scroll; a native of Muzhou; passed the jinshi examination in the Dali era.
translations.idiomatic: Poems of Qu Xinling, 1 scroll; Poems of Zhang Bayuan, 1 scroll; both from Muzhou; Zhang passed the jinshi in the Dali era.

sentences.zh: 秦系詩一卷陳詡集十卷字載物，福州閩縣人。

translations.literal: Qin Xi, Poems, one scroll; Collected Works of Chen Xu, ten scrolls; courtesy name Zaiwu; a native of Min county in Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Xi, Poems, 1 scroll; Collected Works of Chen Xu, 10 scrolls; courtesy name Zaiwu; from Min county, Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 貞元戶部郎中，知制誥。

translations.literal: In the Zhenyuan era he was Director in the Ministry of Revenue and drafted imperial edicts.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhenyuan he served as director in the Ministry of Revenue and as a drafter of edicts.

sentences.zh: 錢起詩一卷李端詩集三卷韓翃詩集五卷司空曙詩集二卷盧綸詩集十卷耿湋詩集二卷崔峒詩一卷韋應物詩集十卷許經邦詩集一卷建中右武衞冑曹參軍。

translations.literal: Qian Qi, Poems, one scroll; Collected Works of Li Duan, three scrolls; Collected Works of Han Hong, five scrolls; Collected Works of Sikong Shu, two scrolls; Collected Works of Lu Lun, ten scrolls; Collected Works of Geng Wei, two scrolls; Cui Tong, Poems, one scroll; Collected Works of Wei Yingwu, ten scrolls; Collected Works of Xu Jingbang, one scroll; Vice Director of the Right Martial Guard in the Jianzhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Qian Qi, Poems, 1 scroll; Li Duan, Collected Works, 3 scrolls; Han Hong, 5 scrolls; Sikong Shu, 2 scrolls; Lu Lun, 10 scrolls; Geng Wei, 2 scrolls; Cui Tong, Poems, 1 scroll; Wei Yingwu, Collected Works, 10 scrolls; Xu Jingbang, Collected Works, 1 scroll; he was Vice Director of the Right Martial Guard in the Jianzhong era.

sentences.zh: 韋渠牟詩集十卷諫議大夫時集。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Wei Qumou, ten scrolls; a collection from when he was Remonstrance Official.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Works of Wei Qumou, 10 scrolls; poems gathered while he was remonstrance official.

sentences.zh: 劉商詩集十卷貞元比部郎中。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Liu Shang, ten scrolls; Director in the Bureau of Punishments in the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Works of Liu Shang, 10 scrolls; he was director in the Bureau of Punishments under Zhenyuan.

sentences.zh: 王建集十卷大和陝州司馬。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Wang Jian, ten scrolls; Secretary of Shanzhou in the Dahe era.
translations.idiomatic: Collected Works of Wang Jian, 10 scrolls; he was secretary of Shanzhou in the Dahe era.

sentences.zh: 張碧謌行集二卷貞元人。

translations.literal: Zhang Bi, Songs and Ballads Collection, two scrolls; a man of the Zhenyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Bi, Songs and Ballads Collection, 2 scrolls; a Zhenyuan-era poet.

sentences.zh: 雍裕之詩一卷楊巨源詩一卷字景山，大和河中少尹。

translations.literal: Yong Yuzhi, Poems, one scroll; Yang Juyuan, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Jingshan; Vice Governor of Hezhong in the Dahe era.
translations.idiomatic: Poems of Yong Yuzhi, 1 scroll; Poems of Yang Juyuan, 1 scroll; courtesy name Jingshan; served as vice governor of Hezhong in the Dahe era.

sentences.zh: 孟郊詩集十卷張籍詩集七卷李涉詩一卷李賀集五卷李紳追昔遊詩三卷又批答一卷章孝標詩一卷殷堯藩詩一卷元和進士第。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Meng Jiao, ten scrolls; Collected Works of Zhang Ji, seven scrolls; Li She, Poems, one scroll; Collected Works of Li He, five scrolls; Li Shen, Recalling Past Travels, three scrolls; another scroll of memorial replies; Zhang Xiaobiao, Poems, one scroll; Yin Yaofan, Poems, one scroll; passed the jinshi examination in the Yuanhe era.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Jiao, Collected Works, 10 scrolls; Zhang Ji, Collected Works, 7 scrolls; Li She, Poems, 1 scroll; Li He, Collected Works, 5 scrolls; Li Shen, Recalling Past Travels, 3 scrolls, plus 1 scroll of memorial replies; Zhang Xiaobiao, Poems, 1 scroll; Yin Yaofan, Poems, 1 scroll; Yin passed the jinshi in the Yuanhe era.

sentences.zh: 李敬方詩一卷字中虔，大和歙州刺史。

translations.literal: Li Jingfang, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Zhongqian; Prefect of Shezhou in the Dahe era.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jingfang, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Zhongqian; prefect of Shezhou in the Dahe era.

sentences.zh: 玉川子詩一卷盧仝。

translations.literal: Master Yuchuan, Poems, one scroll; Lu Tong.
translations.idiomatic: Master Yuchuan, Poems, 1 scroll; that is, Lu Tong.

sentences.zh: 裴夷直詩一卷施肩吾詩集十卷姚合詩集十卷韓琮詩一卷字成封，大中湖南觀察使。

translations.literal: Pei Yizhi, Poems, one scroll; Collected Works of Shi Jianwu, ten scrolls; Collected Works of Yao He, ten scrolls; Han Cong, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Chengfeng; Observation Commissioner of Hunan in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Yizhi, Poems, 1 scroll; Shi Jianwu, Collected Works, 10 scrolls; Yao He, Collected Works, 10 scrolls; Han Cong, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Chengfeng; observation commissioner of Hunan in the Dazhong era.

sentences.zh: 李商隱樊南甲集二十卷乙集二十卷玉溪生詩三卷又賦一卷文一卷賈島長江集十卷又小集三卷張祜詩一卷字承吉，為處士，大中中卒。

translations.literal: Li Shangyin, Fan'an Collection A, twenty scrolls; Collection B, twenty scrolls; Master Yuxi, Poems, three scrolls; another scroll of fu; one scroll of prose; Jia Dao, Yangtze River Collection, ten scrolls; another Small Collection, three scrolls; Zhang Hu, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Chengji; was a recluse scholar; died in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Li Shangyin, Fan'an Collection A, 20 scrolls, and Collection B, 20 scrolls; Master Yuxi, Poems, 3 scrolls, plus 1 scroll of fu and 1 of prose; Jia Dao, Yangtze River Collection, 10 scrolls, with a supplementary Small Collection of 3 scrolls; Zhang Hu, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Chengji; lived as a recluse scholar and died in the Dazhong period.

sentences.zh: 許渾丁卯集二卷字用晦，圉師之後，大中睦州、郢州二刺史。

translations.literal: Xu Hun, Dingmao Collection, two scrolls; courtesy name Yonghui; a descendant of Yu Shi; Prefect of Muzhou and Yingzhou in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Hun, Dingmao Collection, 2 scrolls; courtesy name Yonghui; a descendant of Yu Shi; served as prefect of Muzhou and Yingzhou in the Dazhong era.

sentences.zh: 李遠詩集一卷字求古，大中建州刺史。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Li Yuan, one scroll; courtesy name Qiugu; Prefect of Jianzhou in the Dazhong era.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yuan, Collected Works, 1 scroll; courtesy name Qiugu; prefect of Jianzhou in the Dazhong era.

sentences.zh: 雍陶詩集十卷字國鈞，大中八年自國子毛詩博士出為簡州刺史。

translations.literal: Collected Works of Yong Tao, ten scrolls; courtesy name Guojun; in the eighth year of Dazhong he left his post as Erudite of the Mao Odes at the Directorate of Education to become Prefect of Jianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yong Tao, Collected Works, 10 scrolls; courtesy name Guojun; in 854 he left the post of erudite of the Mao Odes at the Directorate of Education to become prefect of Jianzhou.

sentences.zh: 朱慶餘詩一卷名可久，以字行。

translations.literal: Zhu Qingyu, Poems, one scroll; personal name Kejiu; known by his courtesy name.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Qingyu, Poems, 1 scroll; personal name Kejiu; he was known by his courtesy name.

sentences.zh: 寶曆進士第。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the Baoli era.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi in the Baoli period.

sentences.zh: 喻鳧詩一卷開成進士第，烏程令。

translations.literal: Yu Fu, Poems, one scroll; passed the jinshi examination in the Kaicheng era; Magistrate of Wucheng.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Fu, Poems, 1 scroll; a Kaicheng jinshi; magistrate of Wucheng.

sentences.zh: 馬戴詩一卷字虞臣，會昌進士第。

translations.literal: Ma Dai, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Yuchen; passed the jinshi examination in the Huichang era.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Dai, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Yuchen; a Huichang jinshi.

sentences.zh: 李羣玉詩三卷後集五卷字文山，澧州人。

translations.literal: Li Qunyu, Poems, three scrolls; Later Collection, five scrolls; courtesy name Wenshan; a native of Lizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qunyu, Poems, 3 scrolls, and a Later Collection of 5 scrolls; courtesy name Wenshan; from Lizhou.

sentences.zh: 裴休觀察湖南，厚延致之，及為相，以詩論薦，授校書郎。

translations.literal: When Pei Xiu observed Hunan he warmly invited him; when he became Chancellor he recommended him through a discourse on poetry and appointed him Proofreader.
translations.idiomatic: While serving as observation commissioner of Hunan, Pei Xiu treated him generously; when Pei became chancellor he recommended him in a poetic memorial and appointed him proofreader.

sentences.zh: 崔櫓無譏集四卷郁渾百篇集一卷渾常應百篇舉，壽州刺史李紳命百題試之。

translations.literal: Cui Hu, Collection Without Ridicule, four scrolls; Yu Hun, Hundred-Poem Collection, one scroll; Hun often responded to the hundred-poem examination; Li Shen, Prefect of Shouzhou, ordered a hundred topics to test him.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Hu, Collection Without Ridicule, 4 scrolls; Yu Hun, Hundred-Poem Collection, 1 scroll; Hun often entered the hundred-poem examination, and Li Shen, prefect of Shouzhou, set him a hundred topics as a trial.

sentences.zh: 姚鵠詩一卷字居雲，會昌進士第。

translations.literal: Yao Hu, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Juyun; passed the jinshi examination in the Huichang era.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Hu, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Juyun; a Huichang jinshi.

sentences.zh: 項斯詩一卷字子遷，江東人，會昌丹徒尉。

translations.literal: Xiang Si, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Ziqian; a native of Jiangdong; District Defender of Dantu in the Huichang era.
translations.idiomatic: Xiang Si, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Ziqian; from Jiangdong; defender of Dantu in the Huichang era.

sentences.zh: 孟遲詩一卷字遲之，會昌進士第。

translations.literal: Meng Chi, Poems, one scroll; courtesy name Chizhi; passed the jinshi examination in the Huichang era.
translations.idiomatic: Meng Chi, Poems, 1 scroll; courtesy name Chizhi; a Huichang jinshi.

sentences.zh: 顧非熊詩一卷況之子，大中盱眙簿，棄官隱茅山。

translations.literal: Gu Feixiong, Poems, one scroll; son of Kuang; Registrar of Xuyi in the Dazhong era; abandoned office and lived in seclusion on Mount Mao.
translations.idiomatic: Gu Feixiong, Poems, 1 scroll; son of Gu Kuang; registrar of Xuyi in the Dazhong era; he resigned and lived as a recluse on Mount Mao.

sentences.zh: 章碣詩一卷趙嘏渭南集三卷又編年詩二卷字承祐，大中渭南尉。

translations.literal: Zhang Jie, Poems, one scroll; Zhao Gu, Weinan Collection, three scrolls; another Chronological Poems, two scrolls; courtesy name Chengyou; District Defender of Weinan in the Dazhong era.
